whatIsATrick.title: What is a trick?
whatIsATrick.body: A trick is one round of card play. Each player plays one card in turn. The player who played the strongest card wins the trick — they collect all the cards played and start the next trick.
whatIsATrick.goal: The goal: predict how many tricks you will win before the round starts.

cardValues.title: Card Values
cardValues.body: Cards rank by face value. The Ace is the lowest card (worth 1) and the King is the highest.
cardValues.trump: If a trump suit is in play, any trump card beats any non-trump card, regardless of value.

theDeal.title: Rounds & The Deal
theDeal.body: The game is played over many rounds. Each round has a Dealer — the role passes to the next player after each round.
theDeal.dealIntro: The dealer deals cards one by one to each player, mixing face-up and face-down:
theDeal.bullet1: Face-down cards go into the player's hand — only they can see them.
theDeal.bullet2: Face-up cards stay on the table in front of the player — everyone can see them.
theDeal.bullet3: Every player receives the same total number of cards.
theDeal.bullet4: We recommend at least 5 cards per player in total.
theDeal.trumpBody: After dealing, the dealer may flip the top card of the remaining deck — its suit becomes the trump suit for this round. Trump cards beat everything else.
theDeal.tip: Good starting point: 4 face-up + 5 face-down cards per player.

contracts.title: Contracts
contracts.body: Before any cards are played, each player declares their contract — how many tricks they think they will win. Players declare starting with the player to the left of the dealer, going around the table.
contracts.constraintBody: The dealer goes last and must choose a number that makes the total of all contracts different from the number of tricks in the round. This ensures at least one player will always lose points.
contracts.example: Example: 4 players, 9 tricks. If the first 3 bid 2 + 3 + 2 = 7, the dealer cannot bid 2 (total would be 9). They must bid anything else.

playingARound.title: Playing a Round
playingARound.body: The player to the left of the dealer leads the first trick. Each player must play a card of the same suit as the first card played — this is the most important rule.
playingARound.noSuitIntro: If you have no card of that suit, you may:
playingARound.option1: Play any other non-trump card — this card cannot win the trick.
playingARound.option2: Play a trump card — this beats all non-trump cards.
playingARound.footer: The player who played the highest card wins the trick and leads the next one. You are allowed to start a trick with a trump card.

scoring.title: Scoring
scoring.metTitle: ✓ You won exactly what you bid
scoring.metBody: +1, plus the number of tricks you won
scoring.missedTitle: ✗ You won more or fewer than you bid
scoring.missedBody: −1, minus how far off you were
scoring.summary: Your total score is the sum of all round scores.

winning.title: Winning
winning.body: There is no fixed end condition. The game stops whenever the group decides — when the bar is closing, when a player has to leave, or simply when everyone agrees to stop.
winning.footer: When the game ends, the player with the highest total score wins.
